hypothesis: A gate NIS <= chi2_m(p) on the correctly normalized innovation rejects valid readings at rate 1 - p when the decision does not feed back; closed-loop gating inflates the rate because a rejection preserves the large prior error that caused it.
input_data: 400 runs x 100 ticks = 40000 decisions per gate
mathematical_model: NIS = nu^T S^-1 nu ~ chi2(2), independent across ticks for the optimal filter (white innovations); rejections ~ Binomial(N, 1 - p). Gates: chi2_2(p) = -2 ln(1 - p).
numerical_result: open p=0.9: 0.1016; open p=0.99: 0.0106; open p=0.999: 0.0014; closed p=0.9: 0.1352; closed p=0.99: 0.0113; session gate over p=0.9: 534 rejections, 0 decisions differing, p=0.99: 42 rejections, 0 decisions differing; raw-R gate at 0.99: 0.037.
observation_model: Camera position every tick; no outliers.
